title: Flat local maps with regular source and fibre have regular target
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that $R$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], that the closed fibre $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular, and that $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $S$ is regular.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre); its proof uses Lemma Tag 00ON (dimension-base-fibre-equals-total)

proof.text: Notation and the closed fibre. Write $\varphi:R\to S$, $\mathfrak m_R,\mathfrak m_S$ for the maximal ideals. Since $\varphi$ is local, $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subset\mathfrak m_S$, so $\mathfrak m_RS\subset\mathfrak m_S\ne S$ and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$ (the preimage is a proper ideal containing $\mathfrak m_R$). Hence $\bar S:=S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is a nonzero ring; it is Noetherian as a quotient of the Noetherian ring $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian], and it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS$, since its ideals are the ideals of $S$ containing $\mathfrak m_RS$ and $\mathfrak m_S$ is the only maximal one among them. So the hypothesis '$S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular' is the statement that the Noetherian local ring $\bar S$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre), lines 27458--27468: the setting of the statement, made explicit

proof.text: Dimension formula (Stacks 00ON, which the proof of 031E cites). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map $\varphi$ of Noetherian rings with $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak m_S$ and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$ (Step 1): $\dim S_{\mathfrak m_S}=\dim R_{\mathfrak m_R}+\dim(S_{\mathfrak m_S}/\mathfrak m_RS_{\mathfrak m_S})$. In a local ring every element outside the maximal ideal is a unit, so the localization maps $R\to R_{\mathfrak m_R}$ and $S\to S_{\mathfrak m_S}$ are isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $S_{\mathfrak m_S}/\mathfrak m_RS_{\mathfrak m_S}=S/\mathfrak m_RS=\bar S$. Hence $\dim S=\dim R+\dim\bar S$. (In the height form: $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak m_S=\dim S$, $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak m_R=\dim R$ and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS)=\dim\bar S$, the height of the maximal ideal of a local ring being its dimension.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031E, first sentence (lines 27471--27473), citing Lemma Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total, lines 27420--27456)

proof.text: Generators of $\mathfrak m_S$. Let $d=\dim R$ and $e=\dim\bar S$, both finite natural numbers because $R$ and $\bar S$ are regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Since $R$ is regular, pick $x_1,\dots,x_d$ generating $\mathfrak m_R$; since $\bar S$ is regular, pick $y_1,\dots,y_e\in\mathfrak m_S$ whose images generate the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS$ of $\bar S$ (lift any $e$ generators; the lifts lie in $\mathfrak m_S$). Then $\varphi(x_1),\dots,\varphi(x_d),y_1,\dots,y_e$ generate $\mathfrak m_S$: they lie in $\mathfrak m_S$; and for $s\in\mathfrak m_S$ write $\bar s=\sum_j\bar b_j\bar y_j$ in $\bar S$, so $s-\sum_jb_jy_j\in\mathfrak m_RS=\sum_i\varphi(x_i)S$ (as the $x_i$ generate $\mathfrak m_R$), i.e. $s\in(\varphi(x_1),\dots,\varphi(x_d),y_1,\dots,y_e)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031E, lines 27474--27479

proof.text: Conclusion. By Step 3 the maximal ideal of the Noetherian local ring $S$ is generated by $d+e$ elements, and $d+e=\dim R+\dim\bar S=\dim S$ by Step 2. So $\mathfrak m_S$ can be generated by $\dim S$ elements, which is the definition of a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]; $S$ is regular. (No appeal to the inequality $\dim S\le$ minimal number of generators of $\mathfrak m_S$, Stacks 00KW, is needed, since the definition asks only for generation by $\dim S$ elements.)
